issues.legal_issue: Permission from a competent authority for alienation is not a prerequisite to filing a suit for specific performance.
material_facts: The claimants alleged that a concluded contract for sale existed and that the other side had refused to perform it.
The claimants later relied on learning that the competent authority had granted permission for the sale of the trust property.
issues.conclusion: The authority’s permission was not a condition precedent to filing a suit for specific performance; any decree could be made subject to obtaining that permission.
issues.legal_principle: A claim for specific performance may be brought before permission for the transfer is obtained, and the decree may be made subject to the grant of permission by the competent authority. The judgment cites no earlier case or statutory provision for this proposition.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an alleged agreement to transfer property.
predicates.transfer_requires_authority_permission: A competent authority's permission is required for the proposed property transfer.
predicates.permission_not_precondition_to_suit: The required permission is not a prerequisite to filing the suit for specific performance.

issues.definition: When a suit seeks specific performance of a transfer requiring authority permission, the suit may be filed without first obtaining that permission.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment adding a claim for specific performance is barred when the claim was apparent from the original pleadings but the amendment is sought after the limitation period has expired.
material_facts: The original suit sought a permanent injunction and alleged that a concluded contract for sale existed, that the other side had refused to perform it, and that the claimants were ready and willing to perform their part.
The original plaint did not seek specific performance, although the pleaded refusal was identified as a cause of action.
The claimants sought to amend the plaint to add specific performance about seven years after filing the suit.
The applicable limitation period for the specific-performance claim was three years.
The claimants relied on a later discovery that the competent authority had granted permission for the sale.
issues.conclusion: The amendment application was barred by limitation, and the petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an amendment cannot be used on these facts to defeat the valuable limitation right accrued to the opposing party. Article 54 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963, provided a three-year limitation period. A.K. Gupta v. D.V.C. (1966 (1) SCR 796) did not apply because the claimant there had expressly reserved the right to claim the amount in the original plaint, whereas no comparable reservation was made here.

predicates.pending_suit_amendment_request: A party seeks to amend the pleadings in a pending suit.
predicates.original_pleadings_show_concluded_contra: The original pleadings state that a concluded contract existed and that the opposing party refused to perform it.
predicates.specific_performance_omitted_from_origin: The original claim does not seek specific performance despite pleading facts supporting that relief.
predicates.amendment_sought_after_limitation_expire: The party seeks the amendment after the limitation period for the omitted claim has expired.
predicates.specific_performance_amendment_barred_by: The amendment adding specific performance is barred by limitation.

issues.definition: When a party seeks an amendment in a pending suit, the original pleadings show a concluded contract and refusal, specific performance was omitted, and the amendment is sought after limitation has expired, the amendment is barred by limitation.
